title: runtime: export kernel selection debug info for perf-canary (kernel_id + fallback_reason)
author: Hiro Tanaka
body: Summary: This PR adds a low-overhead export of kernel-selection details (selected kernel id + fallback reason) for perf regression canary traffic, to improve attribution when we see p95 latency or tokens/sec regressions. The export is gated on the request-scoped canary tag (source=perf-canary) so we don’t pay overhead or increase label cardinality for customer traffic. Motivation/Context: In early perf-canary prototyping we saw regressions that were hard to triage because we couldn’t tell whether we were using the expected fast-path kernel or a compatibility fallback (e.g., attention kernel fallback due to shape constraints, quantization mismatch, or driver capability check). Offline benchmark-lab catches many issues, but production fleet heterogeneity + autotune drift can cause kernel changes that only show up in prod slices (GPU SKU, driver, runtime build). This PR adds structured debug context only for canary requests to reduce time-to-triage and to allow dashboards/alerts to link regressions to kernel selection changes. Design: 1) New request-scoped debug blob emitted at the end of request execution (prefill and decode separately) containing: selected_kernel_id (stable short id), selected_kernel_family (coarse enum), fallback_reason (coarse enum), fallback_stage (enum: compile-time, runtime-capability, shape-guard, allocator, other). 2) Gating: only emit when request_context.source == "perf-canary" AND runtime flag enable_canary_kernel_debug=true. This is intentionally double-gated so we can disable quickly if we see unexpected overhead. 3) Cardinality controls: kernel_id is stable and bounded (from a registry), fallback_reason is an enum (no raw strings). We explicitly do not include full shape strings, full kernel names, or compile logs. 4) Export path: a) tracing: add span attributes on the existing inference span (prefill_kernel_id, decode_kernel_id, prefill_fallback_reason, decode_fallback_reason) for perf-canary only; b) metrics: emit a counter kernel_selection_total{source="perf-canary", model, gpu_sku, kernel_family, fallback_reason} with rate-limiting/sampling (1 per N requests) to keep volume bounded. The p95/tokens/sec time series remain unchanged; this is purely for debug drill-down. What changed (high level): - Added KernelSelectionDebug struct + enum definitions for fallback reasons - Added kernel selection registry id mapping (stable ids) - Hooked selection decisions in attention and matmul dispatch paths to record selected kernel id + fallback reason - Added perf-canary gating in request context and debug emission - Added sampling in metric emission path + tests for cardinality constraints Implementation notes: - Kernel IDs are sourced from a compile-time registry (constexpr table) to keep them stable across builds and avoid dynamic string allocations. - Fallback reason mapping is intentionally coarse; the goal is to answer “why did we not use the fast path?” without leaking internal details or exploding labels. - The debug fields are attached after selection finalization so they reflect the effective kernel actually used (not the candidate). - No customer prompts/data is logged; these fields contain only runtime/kernel metadata. Testing: - Unit tests for fallback_reason enum mapping and kernel id registry invariants - Integration test to ensure canary gating prevents emission for non-canary traffic - Metrics label-schema test (ensures only allowed labels appear, fallback_reason bounded to enum set) Rollout/Operational: - This will be used by the perf regression canary service to attach kernel selection context to alerts/dashboards. - If we see overhead or label issues, disable via runtime flag enable_canary_kernel_debug=false without redeploying canary. Checklist: [x] Gated behind canary traffic + runtime flag [x] Bounded label cardinality (enum reasons; stable ids) [x] Added tests for gating + schema [x] Added brief docs to runtime instrumentation notes (internal) Related: - ENG-2844 (runtime instrumentation for canary attribution) - ENG-2841 (Perf regression canary in prod) Notes for reviewers: Please pay special attention to (a) any hidden allocations in hot paths when canary tag is enabled, and (b) the fallback reason taxonomy being useful but not too granular.
commits: runtime/kernel-debug: add KernelSelectionDebug + fallback reason enums
runtime/dispatch: record selected kernel id + fallback stage in attention/matmul selectors
runtime/request-context: gate debug export behind source=perf-canary and enable_canary_kernel_debug
telemetry: add kernel_selection_total metric (canary-only) + sampling guard
tests: add gating + schema/cardinality tests for kernel debug export
review_conversation: Noah Patel (2026-01-22): Love the direction. Two asks: (1) Please ensure kernel_id is bounded/stable across builds (avoid full kernel name strings). (2) Can we separate prefill vs decode to avoid confusion in triage?
Hiro Tanaka (2026-01-22): Updated to use the selection registry for stable ids (no dynamic strings). Added separate fields for prefill/decode in both tracing attrs and the debug struct.

Thomas Baird (2026-01-23): Cardinality looks mostly OK, but I’m worried about fallback_reason being free-form. Can we make it an enum and enforce it in tests? Also, please don’t add model_revision as a label here.
Hiro Tanaka (2026-01-23): Agreed. Converted fallback_reason to a fixed enum + added schema test to assert only allowed label keys. No model_revision label added.
Logan Wright (2026-01-23): Metrics side: emitting a counter per request might be noisy. Can we sample (e.g., 1/20) and keep it canary-only? Tracing attrs are probably enough for per-request details.
Hiro Tanaka (2026-01-23): Added sampling (default 1/25) and made metrics emission conditional on canary + flag. Tracing remains per-request but only for canary traffic.

Omar El-Sayed (2026-01-24): One more nit: please attach the attributes after selection finalization so we don’t record a candidate kernel that gets overridden later. Also watch allocations when formatting.
Hiro Tanaka (2026-01-24): Fixed: record the final selected kernel at the execution boundary, and removed string formatting in hot path (all ids/enums).
Noah Patel (2026-01-24): Approved. This will help a ton with canary regressions.
Thomas Baird (2026-01-24): Approved after enum + schema tests.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash merge. Post-merge note: canary flag enable_canary_kernel_debug remains off by default; will be enabled selectively during perf-canary rollout.
